note: Superseded load_test.py's own same-thread-turns aiohttp mode: that mode's conversation-id extraction from the raw SSE 'response.created' event body returned null for direct aiohttp POSTs (the platform only returns a non-null conversation object via azd's own client-session negotiation, not a bare stream:true POST), so its 4 'follow-up' requests each silently started a NEW conversation instead of reusing one -- see README.md 'Known limitation' section. This file records the corrected same-thread test, run via two concurrent `azd ai agent invoke --session-id <same-guid>` processes (PowerShell Start-Job, truly concurrent OS processes) instead.

results.message: Turn A: what's the status of the investigation?
Turn B: any anomalies found yet?

observation: Both concurrent requests against the same conversation ID completed independently in ~20s each (matching the single-request baseline latency from sequential-cold-start-3.json), not stacked to ~40s. This indicates the platform did NOT observably serialize/queue the two same-thread turns behind one another with material added delay, and neither request errored or was rejected. Both responses were coherent and each addressed its own distinct message -- no evidence of state corruption or cross-talk between the two concurrent turns was observed in this single trial.
